Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Tools and Techniques for Better Timing.
You don’t need anything fancy to put the science of timing to work in your daily life. In fact, some of the most effective changes come from simple tools and habits.
It all starts with paying attention—just observing, trying things out, and making tweaks based on what feels right for you or your team.
Here’s one of my favorite approaches: keeping a timing journal. Imagine jotting down your energy, your mood, and your productivity at different points during the day. Over time, you start to see patterns—maybe you notice you’re sharpest mid-morning, or you dip a bit after lunch. This kind of insight can really help you decide when to dive into challenging work, when to take a breather, or even when to catch up with friends.
Another helpful tool is a daily template. Think of it as a flexible schedule, where you block out time for focused work, routine tasks, breaks, and even creative projects. It’s not set in stone—you can adjust it whenever you need to—but it gives you a solid starting point for matching your activities with your natural rhythms.
If you’re working with a team or in an organization, shared calendars and regular check-ins can make a big difference. They help everyone coordinate schedules, making sure meetings or deadlines happen when folks are at their best. And don’t forget about technology—there are plenty of apps that prompt you to take breaks, track your habits, or even analyze your sleep so you can fine-tune your routines.
So, what are some practical tools you can try out?
First, keep a daily log of your energy, mood, and productivity. This’ll help you spot your own unique patterns.
Next, create a daily template that matches your tasks to your energy levels—so you’re not fighting against your natural flow.
Use reminders or apps to nudge you into taking regular breaks and sticking with healthy routines.
And, coordinate your schedule with others whenever you can. That way, you’ll boost collaboration and avoid unnecessary conflicts.
The most important thing to remember? Experimentation is key. What works great for someone else might not be quite right for you—and that’s totally fine. Life changes, and your routines might need to shift, too. Stay curious, pay attention to what happens, and don’t be afraid to make small tweaks.
That’s how you’ll find your own sweet spot for better timing.
